breaks_down.label: Gravity
breaks_down.text: Earth's gravity is 6.1 times stronger. Loads, traction, dust settling and human movement all differ.

breaks_down.label: Air pressure
breaks_down.text: The Moon has no atmosphere. Vacuum effects on lubricants, seals, dust and heat rejection need a chamber, not a field site.

breaks_down.label: Temperature
breaks_down.text: Lunar surface temperatures are set by sunlight and radiation to space with no air to moderate them. No place on Earth spans this range, so temperature is not scored for the Moon.

breaks_down.label: Radiation
breaks_down.remedy: Needs radiation testing in a laboratory
breaks_down.source: Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances 6, eaaz1334
breaks_down.text: With no global magnetic field and little or no air, surface radiation is far higher than anywhere on Earth: 1.37 mSv a day was measured at Von Kármán crater by the LND instrument on the Chang'E-4 lander, 2019 (Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances 6, eaaz1334), about 210 times the average natural background on Earth (UNSCEAR 2008 Report: 2.4 mSv a year). These are published reference measurements at one place, not values for this site. RADIUM holds no radiation map and does not score it.

breaks_down.label: Water and life
breaks_down.remedy: Cannot be removed in the field
breaks_down.text: This Earth cell has 81 mm of precipitation a year and a peak vegetation index of 0.09. Liquid water, weathering and microbes alter rock and soil in ways that have no counterpart at the planetary site.

breaks_down.label: Length of day
breaks_down.remedy: Needs simulated lighting and thermal cycles
breaks_down.text: Thermal cycling and lighting follow a different rhythm.
